# federation-entity

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from libs/openid-federation/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/federation-entity.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `federation-entity` component of `libs/openid-federation`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.federation`: generated from its catalogue, federation-entity.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Families: `OIDF_FEDERATION_`. A name under one of these that no catalogue declares is an unknown key.

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `FEDERATION`, `HOSTING` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_ANCHORS` (init-param `trustAnchorIssuers`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_TRUST_ANCHORS`) | Unset; a list | This entity's superiors, space- or comma-separated Entity Identifiers, published as its authority_hints; with PingFederate's own issuer in the list it is an anchor instead and publishes trust_mark_issuers and trust_mark_owners. An anchor is recognised with or without a trailing slash, and whatever the case of its host | **Doesn't start**: Unset or blank, or an entry that is not an Entity Identifier (an https URL with a host and no query, fragment or user info): the federation servlet does not start, and the reason names the entry | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATES` (init-param `subordinates`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATES`) | Unset; a list | Entities this one vouches for, space- or comma-separated: /federation/fetch issues a statement about each with the keys pinned for it (OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_PINS, or the authority's store under OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_STORE=database), and /federation/list lists them. Under development an entry with no pin is served with the keys its own Entity Configuration lists, with a WARN (finding F-0012) | **Doesn't start**: Under production, an entry with no pinned keys: the federation servlet is FAILED_CONFIG, and the reason names the entries. A bad entry is otherwise not checked, and fails when it is fetched | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_STORE` | `settings`; one of `settings`, `database` | Where the subordinates' pinned keys, Entity Types and Intermediate flag are kept: settings reads them from OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_PINS, and the operator API cannot change them (409); database keeps them in the authority's store (migration V105), where POST /federation/admin/subordinates enrols and changes them | **Doesn't start**: Anything but settings or database, in any case; or database with neither OIDF_AUTHORITY_DATA_STORE_ID nor OIDF_AUTHORITY_JDBC_URL set, or with OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_PINS set: the federation servlet is FAILED_CONFIG | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_ROLLOVER_HOLD_SECONDS` | `86400`; seconds, 60 to 604800 | How long a rollover the subordinate monitor sees is held before it is applied (plan item S7b, database store): a subordinate's Entity Configuration self-signed by a pinned key and listing another set becomes a PENDING change, applied no sooner than this unless an operator approves it early or rejects it. Until then the old pin is served, so a chain through this entity fails from the moment the subordinate signs with a key outside it - confirm the rollover with the subordinate's operator and approve it early, or ask the subordinate to keep signing with an old key for the hold plus one monitor interval plus a Subordinate Statement's lifetime (3600 s). The production profile refuses less than 86400 under the database store, the only one that applies a rollover | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 60 to 604800, or under 86400 under the production profile with the database store: the federation servlet does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_APPROVAL` | `single`; one of `single`, `two-person` | Who may approve a waiting change to a subordinate's pin (plan item S7b, database store): single lets any operator whose token carries oidf.admin.subordinates.approve approve it, the requester included; two-person refuses the operator who asked for it (409 same_actor). Operators are compared by the token's sub - for client credentials the client id - so two people sharing one client are one actor, and one person with two clients passes: it is as strong as the separation of the operator clients | **Doesn't start**: Anything but single or two-person, in any case: the federation servlet and the operator API's subordinate routes do not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS` | `604800`; seconds, 3600 to 2592000 | How long an enrolment or key change asked for through the operator API waits for approval before the subordinate monitor withdraws it (plan item S7b, database store). A held rollover does not expire | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 3600 to 2592000: the federation servlet does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_MONITOR_SECONDS` | `240`; seconds, 30 to 3600 | How often the subordinate monitor looks at each pinned subordinate's Entity Configuration (plan item S7b): under the database store one node fetches it, elected by the federation-subordinate-monitor lease; under the settings store each node judges what its own refresher saw. A held rollover applies only on an observation at most this old | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 30 to 3600: the federation servlet does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_UNREACHABLE_SECONDS` | `900`; seconds, 60 to 86400 | How long since a subordinate's Entity Configuration was last fetched before the monitor calls it UNREACHABLE (plan item S7b), leaving the subordinate-monitor health part DEGRADED; its pin is still served. Under the database store, also how long with no observation at all before health says no node is watching | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 60 to 86400: the federation servlet does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_PINS` | Unset; a JSON object | Each subordinate's pinned Federation Entity Keys, Entity Types and Intermediate flag, as {"<entity id>": {"jwks": {"keys": [...]}, "entity_types": [...], "intermediate": true\|false}}: the keys its Subordinate Statement carries, whatever answers at its URL. Confirm the keys with the subordinate's operator out of band first. Read when OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_STORE is settings | **Doesn't start**: Not one JSON object; an entry whose name is not an Entity Identifier, or with a member other than jwks, entity_types and intermediate; a jwks that is not public keys each with a unique kid; no Entity Type; an intermediate that is not true or false; or set while OIDF_FEDERATION_SUBORDINATE_STORE is database: the federation servlet is FAILED_CONFIG, and the reason names the entry | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_SIGNING_ALG` | `RS256`; one of `RS256`, `PS256`, `ES256`, `ES384` | How this entity signs: its Entity Configuration and every other federation statement, the explicit registration response, and the Trust Marks it issues. RS256 and PS256 sign with PingFederate's current RSA key, ES256 with its current P-256 key and ES384 with its current P-384 key, read again every OIDF_FEDERATION_KEY_REFRESH_SECONDS | **Doesn't start**: Anything but RS256, PS256, ES256 or ES384, in any case: the federation servlet does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_KEY_REFRESH_SECONDS` | `30`; seconds, 0 to 300 | How long a signing key read from PingFederate is used before it is read again, so a key PingFederate rotates signs within this many seconds, without a restart; 0 reads it for every signature. A read that fails leaves the key read before in use for at most 300 seconds more, then signing answers 503 | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 0 to 300: the federation servlet does not start, and nothing that signs with this entity's keys does | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_KEY_ACTIVATION_DELAY_SECONDS` | `3600`; seconds, 0 to 86400 | How long a signing key PingFederate publishes must have been published before this entity signs with it (OpenID Federation 1.0 section 11.2): the key observer adds it to the Entity Configuration's jwks as soon as PingFederate publishes it, and activates it only once it was first seen this many seconds ago, so peers holding a cached configuration have it before anything is signed with it. The default is an Entity Statement's lifetime. Signing lags PingFederate's own key change by this delay; 0 signs with a new key at the observer's next tick | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number of seconds from 0 to 86400: the federation servlet does not start, and nothing that signs with this entity's keys does | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_ORGANIZATION_NAME` (init-param `organizationName`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_ORGANIZATION_NAME`) | Unset | organization_name in this entity's federation_entity metadata | **Not checked**: Published as given | Any | No |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_TYPES` (init-param `clientRegistrationTypes`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_TYPES`) | `automatic,explicit`; a list | What client_registration_types_supported advertises, space- or comma-separated; none advertises neither and omits the registration endpoint, and federation_registration_endpoint is published only with explicit. Advertising only: registration works whatever it says | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, or none beside another word: the federation servlet does not start. Unknown words are published as given | Any | No |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLVE_DISCOVERY` (init-param `resolveDiscovery`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_RESOLVE_DISCOVERY`) | `known`; one of `known`, `any` | Who the resolve endpoint answers for: known, only this entity, its subordinates and the entities it hosts (18.1); any, anyone | **Doesn't start**: Anything but known or any, in any case: the federation servlet does not start | In production only as accepted risk `resolve-any`: `any`; refuses `FEDERATION` | Yes |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_ATTESTER_JWKS` (init-param `attesterJwks`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_ATTESTER_JWKS`) | Unset; a JSON object | The co-hosted attester's public keys, published as oauth_client_attester.jwks so other authorisation servers can trust its attestations through the federation | **Doesn't start**: Not one JSON object, not a JWK Set, or a key that is not public: the federation servlet does not start | Any | Yes |
| `corsEnabled` (init-param) | `true` | Whether the federation endpoints send CORS headers to the origins corsAllowOrigin lists; with none listed they send none either way | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false, in any case: the federation servlet does not start (under development a spelling the reader before 0.6.0 took, such as yes, is read as it read it, false, with a warning) | Any | No |
| `corsAllowOrigin` (init-param) | Unset; a list | The browser origins, such as https://console.example, allowed to read the federation endpoints, space- or comma-separated; unset, no origin is, since peers fetch them from servers. A listed origin gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin naming it, Vary: Origin and the methods, headers and max age below. Until 0.7.0 this was one value sent to every origin, * by default | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing, or an entry that is not http(s)://host[:port] with no path ('*' included): the federation servlet is FAILED_CONFIG at deploy, naming the setting, and its endpoints answer 503. An origin left out is refused by the browser, not by the server | Any | Yes |
| `corsAllowMethods` (init-param) | `GET, OPTIONS` | Access-Control-Allow-Methods on the federation endpoints, sent only to an origin corsAllowOrigin lists | **Not checked**: Sent as given | Any | No |
| `corsAllowHeaders` (init-param) | `Accept, Content-Type` | Access-Control-Allow-Headers on the federation endpoints, sent only to an origin corsAllowOrigin lists | **Not checked**: Sent as given | Any | No |
| `corsMaxAge` (init-param) | `3600`; a whole number | Access-Control-Max-Age on the federation endpoints, in seconds, sent only to an origin corsAllowOrigin lists | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number that fits an int: the federation servlet does not start | Any | No |
| `tokenEndpointAuthMethodsSupported` (init-param) | `private_key_jwt,attest_jwt_client_auth,attest_jwt_client_auth_dpop`; a list | token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported in the openid_provider metadata, space- or comma-separated | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing (a comma alone): the federation servlet does not start. Otherwise published as given | Any | No |
| `clientAttestationSigningAlgValuesSupported` (init-param) | `RS256,PS256,ES256`; a list | client_attestation_signing_alg_values_supported in the openid_provider metadata, space- or comma-separated | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing (a comma alone): the federation servlet does not start. Otherwise published as given | Any | No |
| `clientAttestationPopSigningAlgValuesSupported` (init-param) | `ES256,RS256,PS256`; a list | client_attestation_pop_signing_alg_values_supported in the openid_provider metadata, space- or comma-separated | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing (a comma alone): the federation servlet does not start. Otherwise published as given | Any | No |
| `dpopSigningAlgValuesSupported` (init-param) | `ES256,RS256,PS256`; a list | dpop_signing_alg_values_supported in the openid_provider metadata, space- or comma-separated | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing (a comma alone): the federation servlet does not start. Otherwise published as given | Any | No |
| `clientAttestationFormatsSupported` (init-param) | `jwt`; a list | Read and kept, space- or comma-separated, and never published | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing (a comma alone): the federation servlet does not start. Otherwise it has no effect | Any | No |
| `clientAttestationPopMethodsSupported` (init-param) | `attestation_pop_jwt,dpop_combined`; a list | The attestation proof-of-possession methods the openid_provider metadata advertises, space- or comma-separated | **Doesn't start**: A list of nothing (a comma alone): the federation servlet does not start. Otherwise published as given | Any | No |
| `attestationChallengeEndpointEnabled` (init-param) | `true` | Whether the openid_provider metadata advertises the attestation challenge endpoint | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false, in any case: the federation servlet does not start (under development a spelling the reader before 0.6.0 took, such as yes, is read as it read it, false, with a warning) | Any | No |
| `OIDF_FEDERATION_IGNORE_SSL_ERRORS` (init-param `ignoreSslErrors`, then system property `oidf.federation.ignore.ssl.errors`, then env `OIDF_FEDERATION_IGNORE_SSL_ERRORS`); superseded, still read: `OIDF_TRUST_CONTROLLER_IGNORE_SSL` (system property `oidf.trust.controller.ignore.ssl`, then env `OIDF_TRUST_CONTROLLER_IGNORE_SSL`) | `false` | Whether federation fetches skip certificate checks, for a test federation only: the federation servlet's own (resolve, Trust Mark status), registration's, the OGNL criteria's and attestation's, read as one setting by every one of them (F-0197). The federation servlet also reads its init-param ignoreSslErrors, first; PDP calls always check | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false, in any case, or the superseded name set to a different value: the components that read it do not start (under development a spelling the reader before 0.6.0 took, such as yes, is read as it read it, false, with a warning) | Not in production: `true`; refuses `FEDERATION`, `AUTO_REGISTRATION`, `ATTESTATION_AUTH`, `ATTESTATION_ISSUER`, `HOSTING` | Yes |

## Removed

Still set in the source it was read from, a removed name is refused, naming what replaces it - unless its row says Ignored: a plugin's field whose stored value the plugin ignores, so a configuration saved before the release still imports and the plugin still runs.

| Setting | Read from | Instead | Removed in | When still set |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trustControllerHost` | init-param | Nothing | 0.6.0 | Refused |
| `signingAlgorithm` | init-param | `OIDF_FEDERATION_SIGNING_ALG` | 0.7.0 | Refused |
